headline: UK accuses Iran's IRGC of plotting attack on Fairford airbase, sanctions two citizens
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated the alleged plot was 'almost certainly' directed by the IRGC, vowing to use all powers to counter Iran's actions.
details: The United Kingdom has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind a plot to attack the Fairford airbase. This serious allegation was made by British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, as reported by Al Jazeera.
In response to the alleged conspiracy, the UK has imposed sanctions on two Iranian citizens. Prime Minister Burnham emphasized that such threats on UK territory would not be tolerated.

Burnham stated that Britain would utilize all available powers to address Iran's activities and sources of funding. He also mentioned that new sanctions would be implemented to limit the IRGC's capacity to cause harm.

UK Foreign Minister Ed Miliband confirmed on X that the two Iranian nationals were sanctioned for their involvement in or support of hostile acts on behalf of the Iranian government. Their identities have not been disclosed.

A joint statement was issued by 29 countries, including the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and most European nations, collectively holding Iran responsible for attempting to infiltrate the airbase.

The statement unequivocally declared that attempts to threaten, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce individuals in other countries are unacceptable. This highlights the broad international concern over the alleged plot.

Meanwhile, Iran's Ambassador to the UK, Ali Mousavi, met with British Minister of State for the Middle East, Stephen Dowty, on October 12. During the meeting, Mousavi directly rejected the allegations of Iran's involvement.

The Iranian Ambassador urged British authorities to refrain from making statements without providing concrete evidence. According to Iran's state news agency IRNA, Mousavi informed British officials that Tehran is prepared to cooperate with any investigation.
The Iranian embassy in London had previously dismissed the accusations of Iran's involvement in the incident as baseless and malicious, maintaining a consistent denial of the allegations.

headline_marked: [[CUET VC locked in office for 15 hours]] by protesting students demanding former VC's reinstatement
headline: CUET VC locked in office for 15 hours by protesting students demanding former VC's reinstatement
summary: Students at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) confined the new Vice-Chancellor and others after he broke a lock to enter his office, leading to a medical emergency inside.
details: Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) Vice-Chancellor Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam has been confined to his office for approximately 15 hours by protesting students. The students locked the main gate of the administrative building on Monday afternoon, trapping the VC and others inside.

The protest demands the reinstatement of former Vice-Chancellor Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem. Students allege the new VC broke the administrative building's lock with the help of CUET Chhatra Dal leaders to enter his office on Monday morning.

Upon learning this, students gave the VC until 12 PM to leave. When he failed to do so, they locked the building at 12:30 PM. Along with the VC, 10-11 other individuals, including the president of CUET Chhatra Dal, were also trapped inside.

During the night, a medical emergency arose inside the building. A CUET medical center doctor, Md. Abdullah, was called in and found an engineer, Shahriar, with high blood pressure (170/100 mmHg), recommending his transfer to Chittagong Medical College Hospital.

The VC stated he was well but confirmed two alumni members were suffering from high blood pressure complications. He called for an ambulance and a doctor, noting that everyone inside felt unwell and exhausted from the prolonged confinement.

Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam was appointed CUET VC on September 21. Students had already begun protests against the removal of Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem and demanded his reinstatement, leading to a complete 'shutdown' since September 22.

University teachers, officials, and staff are also observing a work abstention for the same demand. As a result, academic activities, examinations, and other university functions have been suspended for nearly three weeks.
